Abstract: In this study, a novel digital twin (DT) modeling approach is developed to enhance the reliability assessment of civil structures subjected to multi-source uncertainties. Referring to the proposed procedure, a modular Bayesian inference (MBI) with the Transitional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (TMCMC) sampling algorithm is first used to calibrate the DT model of structures based on measured structural responses. Distinguished from the classic Bayesian inference approach, the uncertainty caused by modeling errors is added to the extended likelihood function by using a bias function. Then, the DT model calibration of structures can be achieved by three modules. Based on the calibrated DT model of structures, a finite number of discrete structural response samples can be generated by performing nonlinear dynamic analysis. Then, the generalized extreme value distribution (GEVD) is used to fit the probability density function (PDF) of these discrete response samples based on the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) algorithm. Subsequently, the earthquake-induced failure probability of structures can be assessed by directly integrating the fitted GEVD and predefined structural failure thresholds. Numerical simulations on a three-story steel frame structure subjected to seismic excitations are developed to validate the feasibility of the proposed approach. The shake table tests on a scaled reinforced concrete (RC) column structure are further conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Both numerical and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach is reliable and highly effective for structural reliability assessment. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company

Abstract: Drug-induced QT interval prolongation is a key biomarker of proarrhythmic risk and central to drug cardiac safety evaluation alongside in vitro assays and animal studies, yet current preclinical frameworks provide limited insight into how experimental uncertainty and extreme exposures translate into real-world arrhythmic risk despite both factors critically modulating outcomes. To address this, we used sex-specific machine learning surrogate models trained on 3D cardiac digital twins—mechanistic electrophysiology models of anatomically detailed ventricles that integrate multichannel ion channel block data—combining the realism of 3D simulations with high-throughput capability to enable rapid, ethically unconstrained assessment of proarrhythmic risk. We illustrate the approach using loperamide, which is safe at therapeutic doses but linked to fatal arrhythmias at extreme exposures, through two analyses: propagating experimental (Formula presented) and Hill coefficient variability to quantify its effect on predicted QT prolongation and arrhythmic probability, and simulating extreme exposures to identify sex-specific arrhythmogenic thresholds. Experimental variability substantially broadened uncertainty in predicted QT prolongation across exposure levels, while extreme exposure simulations identified arrhythmogenic thresholds of approximately 107–(Formula presented) in female models and 213–(Formula presented) in male models. This framework provides a scalable, physics-based tool for early-stage drug cardiac safety evaluation. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. Title: Toward reliable physics-informed neural networks under degradation uncertainty: An implicit-volume framework for dynamic modeling of gas turbine engines
Affiliations: The Key Laboratory of Power Machinery and Engineering of Education Ministry, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, 200240, China; Shanghai Jiao Tong University Sichuan Research Institute, Chengdu, 610213, China
Authors with affiliations: Jia X., The Key Laboratory of Power Machinery and Engineering of Education Ministry, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, 200240, China; Zhou D., The Key Laboratory of Power Machinery and Engineering of Education Ministry, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, 200240, China, Shanghai Jiao Tong University Sichuan Research Institute, Chengdu, 610213, China
Abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling of gas turbine engines under real-operating conditions is important for digital-twin assessment and system monitoring. Traditional component-level models rely on repeated nonlinear iterations for dynamic simulation, while standard physics-informed neural networks may suffer robustness degradation when ideal physical priors are inconsistent with degradation-affected data. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes the Implicit Volume Physics-Informed Neural Network (IVP-PINN) to improve dynamic modeling reliability for gas turbine engines under degradation uncertainty. First, a statistical error-tolerance mechanism employing a divergence metric relaxes the zero-residual constraint imposed on the flow-matching relation of the non-degraded reference model, thereby accommodating degradation-induced model mismatch without relaxing the physical mass-conservation law. Second, an implicit-volumetric architecture considering unsteady wave coupling utilizes neural network nonlinear mapping to bypass traditional iterative solvers. This simultaneously substantially reduces the computational cost and preserves authentic volumetric hysteresis effects. Validations under diverse transient disturbances and actual operational data show that IVP-PINN closely captures complex trajectories. Within the validated outside-training degradation range of [−10%, −6%), 87.75% of healthy-state predictive performance was retained at −10%. Compared with PI-LSTM, PINN, and MLP, IVP-PINN reduces peak MaxAE by 58.5%, 71.2%, and 68.0%. The proposed IVP-PINN shows potential for digital-twin dynamic assessment of gas-turbine systems. Abstract: Obtaining accurate wideband full-field vibration responses is essential for structural optimization and health monitoring of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). Traditional full-field sensing schemes rely on high-density sensor arrays, resulting in prohibitive hardware costs and data redundancy. Meanwhile, conventional finite element-based optimal sensor placement (OSP) methods suffer from limited reconstruction fidelity when confronted with complex assembly interfaces and model uncertainties. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a data-driven framework termed “offline full-field calibration-online sparse virtual sensing”. First, using full-field prior data acquired from a high-density sensor array, a sensor topology selection strategy combining principal component analysis (PCA) with Mahalanobis distance-based K-medoids clustering is developed. By introducing Mahalanobis distance for energy-weighted normalization, this strategy effectively decouples strong spatial correlations, preventing high-energy dominant modes from obscuring wideband local dynamic details. Second, to meet the demand for lightweight online sensing, a robust Gappy proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) algorithm with Tikhonov regularization is introduced. This approach effectively suppresses numerical ill-posedness and ensures physical consistency in response inversion. Experimental validation on a 49-sensor stator-housing assembly demonstrates that the proposed strategy achieves a sensor reduction ratio of 87.8% while accurately capturing the dynamic feature manifold. Specifically, the minimalist array robustly achieves a comprehensive full-field average virtual sensing accuracy of 93.5%. This closed-loop framework balances physical insight with economic efficiency, offering a versatile technical pathway for condition awareness in complex rotating machinery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Data-driven perspectives on pyrolysis of heterogeneous solid waste for hydrogen production: A comprehensive review

Abstract: The rapid accumulation of heterogeneous solid waste has created severe pressures on environmental management and resource recovery. Pyrolysis and pyrolysis–reforming can convert complex solid waste streams into hydrogen-rich gas. They are therefore promising pathways for both waste valorization and low-carbon hydrogen production. However, pyrolysis-based hydrogen production is difficult to describe using conventional mechanistic models. The difficulty is driven by feedstock heterogeneity, complex reaction networks, and multiscale reaction–transport coupling. This review examines machine learning (ML) applications in pyrolysis-based hydrogen production from heterogeneous solid waste from a data-driven perspective. Key topics include H₂-related output prediction, key-variable identification, catalyst screening, and operating-condition optimization. Reactor-level support and system assessment assisted by techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) are also discussed. ML can improve prediction and optimization efficiency under controlled data conditions. Nevertheless, insufficient data quality, inconsistent evaluation standards, limited model generalizability, and weak deployment adaptability still constrain its engineering application. Future efforts should strengthen standardized data infrastructures, physics-informed modelling, and uncertainty quantification. Stronger integration among ML, TEA, LCA, digital twins (DTs), and large language models (LLMs) is also needed. These advances will help move pyrolysis-based hydrogen production from laboratory prediction toward engineering scale-up and system deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A Study on Digital Twin Fidelity for Shop Floor Operational Optimization

Abstract: Manufacturing processes and production systems are becoming increasingly sophisticated, while market demand and external conditions are rapidly evolving. In this context, the adoption of digital twin technology has been expanding to maintain manufacturing competitiveness by enabling the prediction of system performance under various uncertainties and the optimization of operational decisions. The accuracy of prediction and analysis based on digital twins largely depends on the fidelity of the digital model, which represents how precisely the real manufacturing system is replicated. In general, high-fidelity models can provide results that closely approximate real-world system behavior. However, such models incur significant simulation time and cost due to increased model complexity and data requirements. As a result, directly applying high-fidelity digital twins to real-world production decision-making remains challenging. This study defines the concept of digital twin fidelity for production operations and proposes a workflow for its systematic design. In particular, digital twin fidelity for production optimization is structured into four dimensions–Geometry, Attribute, Data Synchronization, and Operational Logic–each specified in terms of detailed elements and corresponding levels. The proposed workflow supports the selection of appropriate fidelity levels according to different optimization objectives and operational scenarios. A case study is conducted to validate the proposed workflow by developing a workflow-based low-fidelity digital twin model and applying it to a production optimization problem. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces simulation time compared to a high-fidelity digital twin model, while achieving identical optimization outcomes. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Shift-Robust Quality Prediction in Sugar Crystallization Using Physics-Guided Gradient Boosting
Affiliations: Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia
Authors with affiliations: Martin R.J., Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia; Khawaji A., Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Sugar crystallization is a tightly controlled unit operation in which variations in supersaturation, temperature, and impurity load can directly affect Brix, purity, color, and crystal size. However, data-driven soft sensors often face limited labeled data, measurement noise, missing observations, and poor generalization under changing operating conditions. This study presents a synthetic digital-twin benchmark for vacuum pan crystallization and a physics-guided machine-learning framework based on gradient-boosting decision trees for simultaneous prediction of multiple quality attributes. The benchmark generates batch trajectories using simplified mass–energy balances and crystallization-rate proxies, while incorporating industrially relevant sensor noise, drift, missingness, actuator lag, feed-quality disturbances, and operating-regime shifts. Windowed process histories are transformed into process-informed descriptors and used to train gradient-boosting models for Brix, purity, color, and crystal-size prediction. Physical plausibility was assessed through process-informed features, monotonicity checks, and residual-based scoring, while robustness was evaluated using in-distribution (Test-ID) and out-of-distribution (Test-OOD) scenarios and conformal prediction intervals. The proposed models achieved strong nominal performance for Brix, purity, and crystal size, with Test-ID RMSE values of 0.440, 0.810, and 18.502, respectively. Under operating shifts, Brix and purity remained comparatively stable, whereas color and crystal size showed greater performance degradation, indicating higher sensitivity to regime changes. Conformal analysis provided informative uncertainty estimates under nominal conditions but revealed reduced coverage under Test-OOD conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of gradient-boosting soft sensors for crystallization monitoring while highlighting the need for improved uncertainty quantification and distribution-shift resilience for reliable industrial deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Society for Sugar Research & Promotion 2026.

Abstract: Gasification provides a flexible route for converting coal, biomass, plastics, and waste-derived feedstocks into syngas, hydrogen, fuels, chemicals, power, and carbon materials. Its modeling and operation remain difficult because feedstock composition, reaction regimes, multiphase transport, reactor configuration, sensor availability, and downstream integration vary simultaneously. Machine learning (ML) has consequently expanded from static performance prediction to CFD surrogate modeling, soft sensing, fault diagnosis, predictive control, digital twins, and sustainability assessment. However, the literature remains dominated by application-specific accuracy reports, and R2, RMSE, and MAE values are often compared without accounting for sample size, data provenance, validation strategy, domain shift, uncertainty, or deployment conditions. This review combines a broad Web of Science corpus of 951 records with a 417-record direct-topic sensitivity subset and a separately screened technical evidence layer. It reorganizes the evidence through a system-level framework linking gasification science, descriptor engineering, task–model matching, trustworthy validation, cyber–physical integration, and sustainability-oriented decision making. Representative studies demonstrate large reductions in surrogate-computation time and credible industrial optimization, but few establish closed-loop deployment. In an adjacent solar-thermochemical membrane-reactor study, a learning-assisted feedforward–feedback controller reduced the control integral error by 82.4%, increased hydrogen recovery and yield by 43% and 33%, respectively, and reduced the input preheat ratio by 30%; these results are informative for controller architecture but are not direct gasification evidence. The review proposes gasification-specific descriptor classes, a task–data–model selection matrix, evidence levels for validation and deployment, and a decision chain coupling uncertainty-aware prediction with scenario evaluation, robust Pareto optimization, risk filtering, governed execution, and feedback learning. The central conclusion is that progress depends less on marginal in-distribution accuracy than on transferable, physically consistent, uncertainty-aware, and governed ML systems that convert predictions into verifiable operating and sustainability decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: Background: Advances in the theory and methods of computational oncology have enabled accurate characterization and prediction of tumor growth and treatment response on a patient-specific basis. This capability can be integrated into a digital twin framework in which bi-directional data-flow between the physical tumor and the digital tumor facilitate dynamic model re-calibration, uncertainty quantification, and clinical decision-support via recommendation of optimal therapeutic interventions. However, many digital twin frameworks rely on bespoke implementations tailored to each disease site, modeling choice, and algorithmic implementation. Results: We present TumorTwin, a modular and differentiable software framework for initializing, updating, and leveraging patient-specific cancer tumor digital twins. TumorTwin is publicly available as a Python package, with associated documentation, datasets, and tutorials. Novel contributions include the development of a patient-data structure adaptable to different disease sites, a modular architecture to enable the composition of different data, model, solver, and optimization objects, and CPU or GPU parallelized implementations of forward model solves and gradient computations. We demonstrate the functionality of TumorTwin via an in silico dataset of high-grade glioma growth and response to radiation therapy. Conclusion: The TumorTwin framework enables rapid prototyping and testing of image-guided oncology digital twins. This allows researchers to systematically investigate different models, algorithms, disease sites, or treatment decisions while leveraging robust numerical and computational infrastructure. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Multi-line LiDAR 3D construction environment modeling and BIM consistency update method for digital twins
Affiliations: Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610100, China
Authors with affiliations: Liu C., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; Xu X., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; Ding X., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; He G., Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610100, China
Abstract: Construction digital twins aim to maintain an up-to-date, BIM-consistent as-built state from streaming multi-line LiDAR to enable progress verification, dimensional compliance control, and proactive safety management on construction sites. However, converting sequential LiDAR observations into a temporally stable, element-centric BIM state is difficult in realistic AEC environments. Existing approaches mainly fall into geometry-driven Scan-to-BIM registration frameworks and learning-based point cloud perception models, with some system-level digital-twin frameworks built on BIM-centric reasoning. Purely geometric alignment is brittle under occlusion, clutter, and repetitive structures, and registration uncertainty can propagate to downstream progress and deviation conclusions. Meanwhile, generic perception networks are often trained on static frames, lack temporal stabilization, and do not explicitly optimize BIM-consistent element association or geometry-aware alignment cues. In addition, many digital-twin systems expose limited, loosely coupled state representations that hinder causal, reliable site updates. To address these gaps, we propose LiBiDT (LiDAR–BIM Digital Twin), a causal LiDAR–BIM digital-twin model—where “causal” refers to computational online updating in which only past observations enter the current state—that integrates spatio-temporal mapping, geometric–semantic perception, and scan-to-BIM association for consistent state evolution. LiBiDT consists of Spatio-Temporal Global Registration (STGR) with LiDAR–IMU–GNSS priors, Multi-task Perception (MTP) using a PointNet++ backbone with semantic/instance/normal heads, and Scan-to-BIM Association and State Updating (S2B) via normal-guided point-to-plane refinement, bipartite matching with fused overlap/deviation/semantic evidence, and exponential moving average (EMA) stabilization. The Decision and Risk Analytics (DRA) layer turns the BIM-aligned state into auditable construction-management indicators—weighted completion, deviation summaries, and three forward-evaluable safety/compliance hazard flags. Experiments on three public benchmarks (Hilti SLAM, CV4AEC 2024 Scan-to-BIM, and S3DIS Area-5) cover trajectory, perception, and association evaluation. On CV4AEC 2024 Scan-to-BIM, LiBiDT reaches association F1 = 0.837 and Chamfer Distance (CD) / surface Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 3.2/3.5 cm; relative to the perception-replacement baseline (PointNet++ + S2B, F1 = 0.758) the gain is large, while relative to the strongest competing baseline—CoFiNet (Reg) + S2B at F1 = 0.822—the absolute association gain narrows to 0.015 F1 points, with the bigger gains coming from temporal identity consistency (IDF1 0.854 0.861) and ID-switch reduction. A held-out tile-stream case study visualises BIM-element state evolution, alignment refinement, EMA-stabilised evidence streams, and hazard-flag firing as the scan progressively covers the floor; a strict temporal validation under active construction will require time-stamped multi-acquisition data and is left to future work. Ablation results confirm that evidence stabilization and multi-cue matching contribute complementary gains in accuracy and temporal consistency, yielding a favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-off. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Development and performance analysis of a supercritical carbon dioxide power cycle for scramjet cooling and power generation considering digital twin of heater
Affiliations: Science and Technology on Reactor System Design Technology Laboratory, Nuclear Power Institute of China, Chengdu, 610213, China; College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China
Authors with affiliations: Cao L., Science and Technology on Reactor System Design Technology Laboratory, Nuclear Power Institute of China, Chengdu, 610213, China; Zhou J., College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China; Zhang F., College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China; Liao G., College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China
Abstract: Thermodynamic analyses of supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) power cycles commonly rely on zero-dimensional (0D) or quasi-one-dimensional models that cannot resolve the three-dimensional thermohydraulic behaviour of scramjet cooling channels, whereas full computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for iterative cycle analysis. Here, we develop a CFD-based digital-twin reduced-order model (ROM) of the heater and integrate it into a two-way coupled 0D-3D model of a recuperated onboard sCO2 cycle for scramjet cooling and power generation. CFD predictions agreed with two published experimental datasets within the reported uncertainty bands. The ROM was trained using 24 operating conditions generated by Latin hypercube sampling and tested against nine independent CFD cases. Maximum errors were 0.095%, 0.059%, 0.059%, 0.004%, and 1.157% for average outlet temperature, maximum inner- and outer-wall temperatures, average inlet pressure, and pressure drop, respectively. At identical mass flow rates, the conventional and coupled models predicted similar overall cycle performance, but the conventional model overestimated heater cooling and underestimated maximum wall temperature. The coupled model predicted that the inner- and outer-wall temperatures exceeded 1100 K at sCO2 mass flow rates below 1.75 and 1.80 kg s−1, respectively. Under the same wall-temperature constraint, the conventional model overestimated turbine and net power, thermal efficiency, recuperator mass, and total heat-exchanger mass, while underestimating compressor power, cooling-fuel consumption, cooler mass, and required sCO2 mass flow. The coupled model therefore provides a more reliable basis for performance and thermal-safety assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: nZEB beyond prediction in smart built environments: formalising engineering knowledge through modular explainable machine learning

Abstract: This paper demonstrates how explainable machine learning (XAI) can be operationalised as a methodological pathway for formalising engineering knowledge from high-frequency building operational data. We propose a modular pipeline that combines feature engineering, ensemble and sequence learners, SHAP attribution and uncertainty quantification to convert raw sensor streams into machine-readable knowledge artefacts (JSON schema) suitable for automation workflows such as fault detection and demand response. Using a monitored nearly Zero-Energy Building (nZEB) in Lisbon (12 months, 5-minute resolution), we (i) report model performance (LightGBM, Random Forest, SVR, Linear Regression, and LSTM) under time-aware 70/15/15 split and 5-fold temporal cross-validation; (ii) present SHAP-based global and local attribution analyses that identify stable seasonal drivers; and (iii) provide computational cost (training and inference times) and uncertainty quantification. Results show ensemble models achieve superior short-term forecasting accuracy while producing consistent, actionable attributions that can be encoded as reusable artefacts. We close by describing a JSON artefact schema and outlining how these artefacts could be integrated within digital twins and supervisory control systems. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Dynamic decarbonization pathways for inland shipping under energy system and policy uncertainties
Source title: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment

Abstract: Inland shipping decarbonization requires coordinated changes in fleets, fuels, infrastructure, and policy that static life cycle assessments cannot capture. This study develops a framework coupling Power-to-X pathways, dynamic hybrid life cycle assessment, a fleet digital twin, and multi-objective optimization. Applied to 2,100 weighted representative vessel records in the Yangtze River Delta from 2025 to 2050 under four policy scenarios, the selected integrated policy knee solution reduces diesel from 99.0% to 15.5% of fleet shaft energy demand. Battery electricity becomes the largest low-carbon pathway (30.3%), followed by hydrogen (22.1%), e-methanol (16.4%), and ammonia (15.6%). Cumulative life cycle emissions are 298.8 Mt CO2-eq, 10.4% below business as usual, while net present resource cost is 166.3 billion 2025 USD. Deep inland shipping decarbonization is feasible but back-loaded and depends on coordinated fleet renewal, infrastructure deployment, and fuel diversification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
